title: add VPC control plane provisioning: subnets, endpoints, security groups, peering, DNS (terraform)
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Add a reusable Terraform module and example for provisioning the Redwood Private control-plane VPC topology. This includes subnet layout, AWS VPC endpoints (S3, ECR, STS), security groups for control-plane services, VPC peering and cross-account route provisioning, and Route53 private hosted zone / zone association for service discovery across peered VPCs. This PR is intended to be used by the Private installer (redwood-private-installer) and as a reference for on-prem/cloud deployments. Changes: - New module terraform/modules/vpc-control-plane with main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf, README and examples. - Example usage in terraform/examples/control-plane-vpc to demonstrate single-account and cross-account peering flows. - Small Helm values tweak for redwood-private to expose control-plane DNS names when deploying in private mode. - Docs: docs/private/vpc-control-plane.md with architecture diagrams and upgrade notes. - CI: added terragrunt/terraform validate + plan pipeline for the module. Upgrade notes and rollback: The module is additive by default and creates new subnets and SGs; route table updates for peering are guarded behind a flag (create_peering_routes) to allow a phased rollout. Rollback strategy documented: remove route propagation and peering association before destroying subnets; example rollback script included in examples/. Testing: unit-style terraform validate and fmt, integration Terraform plan in a sandbox AWS account, and an end-to-end smoke test that provisions the example VPC and validates DNS resolution across peered VPCs. Checklist: - [x] Terraform module implemented - [x] Example configurations - [x] Docs and architecture notes - [x] Automated validation in CI - [x] Security review (SG ingress/egress minimal) Known limitations: - Cross-account IAM role creation and full route propagation require operator permissions; example shows recommended least-privilege policies but team must wire their CI credentials. - GCP/Azure provider parity is out of scope for this PR and will be tracked separately (ENG-4410). Related: closes ENG-4382.

merge_commit_message:
Add VPC control-plane provisioning module (subnets, endpoints, SGs, peering, DNS)

- Reusable module with examples and docs
- CI validation and rollback guidance

Closes ENG-4382
release_notes: Added a Terraform module to provision Redwood Private control-plane VPC assets (subnets, managed endpoints, security groups, VPC peering, and Route53 private hosted zones). Includes example configurations, CI validation, and documentation. Notable: cross-account peering and DNS association are supported but require operator IAM setup.
notes_for_ops: When rolling out to existing installations: enable create_peering_routes=false initially, verify DNS resolution and SG policy, then toggle to true to update route tables. Use the included rollback script to safely remove peering before destroying subnets.
scope: terraform module + docs + small helm values change + CI
security_impact: low (adds AWS resources). Security review performed; SGs are restrictive by default and example IAM roles are least-privilege. Operators must audit cross-account IAM/peering policies.
testing_performed: terraform validate/fmt, integration terraform plan in sandbox AWS account, e2e DNS resolution smoke test across peered VPCs, manual security review
associated_manual_steps: For existing installs: 1) run example plan with create_peering_routes=false 2) approve peering in operator account 3) enable create_peering_routes and re-run apply 4) verify private DNS resolution via included validation script
notes: This PR is part of the Private deployment automation workstream and will be consumed by the private-installer. Follow-on work: add provider parity for GCP/Azure (tracked ENG-4410) and integrate the module with the installer’s upgrade orchestration.
